newsitem.title: CHINA: China border guards stop 300 stealing into HK.
newsitem.headline: China border guards stop 300 stealing into HK.

text.p: Chinese border guards have stopped more than 300 people trying to sneak across the border from southern Guangdong province into Hong Kong and China's police chief on Wednesday promised tighter controls.

Between June 23 and July 7, Guangdong police arrested nine "snake heads" -- a term for people smuggling illegal immigrants across the border -- and caught more than 300 people, including 12 children, trying to sneak into Hong Kong by land and sea, the China News Service said.
In one incident on June 23, border guards caught one snake head and a group of 51 people he was trying to smuggle across the border, the news service said.

Public Security Minister Tao Siju had issued a pledge to tighten controls along the border with Hong Kong to clamp down on illegal entry into the crowded former British colony, which reverted to Chinese rule on July 1, the China Daily said.
"We will resolutely punish the law-breakers," Tao was quoted as saying, adding that the police were confident of maintaining border security.
Tao pledged better checks at the Hong Kong and Macau borders and increased border patrols.

He said he hoped for closer ties and better cooperation between mainland police and their counterparts in Hong Kong but pledged not to interfere with the work of the Hong Kong police force, the newspaper said.

China has stepped up controls along the border with Hong Kong in recent weeks to try to halt a flood of illegal immigrants trying to slip into the territory amid rumours of an amnesty after the July 1 handover.
In the first four months of this year, 7,406 illegal immigrants were arrested trying to cross the border, compared with 23,180 for the whole of 1996.
